bullets: Game 6 of 7 in a single-deck session (video t=999-1217 s; the in-game clock OCR failed for the whole video, so all times are video seconds). Opponent played a Lumberloon Freeze list with Evo Inferno Dragon, Evo Electro Dragon, Bowler and Tornado.

Core loop: Goblin Barrel on the enemy left tower almost every cycle (t=1009, 1036, 1088, 1146, 1166, 1182 s, five of six on tile (3,25)) with Wall Breakers in the opposite lane (t=1025, 1061, 1086, 1115, 1164, 1180 s) - "Evo Wall Breakers on the right side and then we can barrel on the left here... Just keep being annoying".
Lane selection is driven by the opponent's splash: "cuz he has the Bowler on the right" (t=1040 s) and "we obviously don't want to give him any value with the Barbarian Barrel" (t=1149 s).

Defence is Bomb Tower plus cheap resets rather than a hard counter: Bomb Tower at (12,3)/(7,9)/(7,10) against Lumberjack, Graveyard and Balloon, with Ice Spirit and Fire Spirit resetting the Evo Inferno Dragon and Royal Delivery cleaning up (t=1071-1076, 1139-1143, 1196-1205 s).

The deck's stated engine in this matchup is Magic Archer volume - "We need to stock up our Magic Archers, like crazy" (t=1109 s) and "As long as we always have one for his 'nado, then we're good" (t=1157 s) - six Magic Archers in ~210 s, mostly placed in the back of his own half.
Ronin is used as a punish/bridge unit rather than the win condition: bridge at (17,11) t=1032 s and (1,14) t=1172 s, defensively at (0,9) against a bad Lumberjack t=1120 s.

Outcome: chip took the opponent's towers to roughly 611-1190 and 1359 HP versus his own 2222 and 4474, but no tower is ever read at 0 and no result is called; his left tower was collapsing under Freeze + Evo Inferno Dragon as the game ended (t=1208-1213 s), so the match file records the result as unknown with the evidence leaning loss.

new_deck.rationale: Two bait win conditions (Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers) played on opposite lanes every cycle, with a cheap 1-elixir spirit shell and no heavy tank.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck wins by never letting the opponent hold a small spell: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are alternated into opposite lanes on nearly every cycle, so whichever answer the opponent keeps, the other half connects. Ryley picks the barrel lane off their splash card - "cuz he has the Bowler on the right" and "we obviously don't want to give him any value with the Barbarian Barrel" - which turns lane choice into a read rather than a habit. Defensively it is a Bomb Tower shell: the building anchors tanks, Balloons and Graveyards while Ice Spirit and Fire Spirit reset an Inferno Dragon and Royal Delivery clears the leftovers, and Ronin is held as a bridge punish or as a parry answer to a mis-placed melee tank. Against heavy-support decks the stated engine is Magic Archer volume - a fresh one down in the back on nearly every rotation so there is always one available after the opponent's Tornado.
